finding: Doc comment asserts 'Keep this as the ONE installation site', but McpChatExtension::new (chat_extension/mcp.rs:810) constructs a second McpSessionManager on the live chat path. A maintainer greps two hits and one comment denying it.
resolution: fixed — comment rewritten in core::app_builder::install_mcp_session_manager to say ONE installation site (Extension + set_global) while naming the chat-extension construction explicitly and the condition under which it becomes harmful

finding: spawn_idle_reaper was moved into the shared installer, adding an always-on 60s timer to the desktop/Tauri process. The pool it scans is provably never populated: the only inserter, get_or_create, has zero callers workspace-wide; every live path uses the ephemeral get_or_create_with_context. New always-on timer for zero behaviour, and outside what INV-1 claims.
resolution: fixed — reaper start removed from the shared path and left in main.rs exactly as before, so the embedded/desktop path gains no timer; its #[allow(dead_code)] markers restored since it is bin-only again

finding: Installer doc claimed 'boot keeps it for close_all() at shutdown', but setup_server binds the handle to _ and run_server serves detached with no graceful-shutdown hook, so close_all is unreachable on that path. Only main.rs calls it. The claim is false for one of the two callers named in the same paragraph.
resolution: fixed — claim removed from the shared doc; lib.rs call site now explains why the handle is dropped and what breaks if pooling is ever rewired

finding: install was not idempotent and failed silently: a second call constructs a new manager, has its OnceLock::set dropped, and layers the NEW one as the Extension while global() keeps returning the FIRST — the exact Extension-vs-global divergence the change exists to prevent, with no diagnostic. Unreachable today (ZieeServerBoot guards double-boot; harnesses spawn child processes) but undefended.
resolution: fixed — build_session_manager returns the already-installed manager on a second call, and returns global() rather than its local Arc so the Extension and global() are the same instance by construction even under a race

oracle: verified by grep: the only fn under src-app/server/src/modules/ taking or returning axum::Router; precedent apply_rate_limit_layer(router, config) lives in the assembly layer
finding: An MCP client-transport module took and returned an axum::Router, inverting the module->assembly dependency (CODING_GUIDELINES §9). Every sibling extension is Extension(module::build_x(..)) — the module yields a value, the assembly layer does the layering (build_auth_context, build_file_context, ZieeIdentityResolver).
resolution: fixed — split into manager::build_session_manager(config) -> Arc<..> (no axum) and core::app_builder::install_mcp_session_manager(router, config), the latter sitting beside apply_rate_limit_layer and create_cors_layer

oracle: axum runs FromRequestParts extractors left-to-right and every handler declares auth: RequirePermissions<..> before Extension(session_manager)
finding: assert_handler_ran only checked 'not 500 / no missing-extension body'. A 401 or 403 short-circuits BEFORE the Extension extractor, so any permission-constant rename, harness group-seeding change, or token-minting break would turn all four tests permanently green with the ship-blocker fully restored.
resolution: fixed — guard added in both test files. Matched on the extractor's error CODES (MISSING_TOKEN / INVALID_TOKEN / INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS) rather than on status, because the handlers themselves also return 403 (USER_NO_ACCESS) from their body, which IS a valid proof

oracle: observed statuses in the GREEN run: 200 for test-connection, 404 for the unknown-id tools call
finding: 'Not 500' is satisfied by a 404/405 from a router that no longer mounts the route, so the tests could not distinguish 'handler ran' from 'route removed'. A free, strictly stronger pin was available.
resolution: fixed — exact statuses asserted (200 for test-connection, 404 for the unknown-id tools call), both confirmed by an actual run rather than assumed

oracle: TestMcpConnectionRequest (modules/mcp/types.rs:148-174) declares no name/display_name and does not deny_unknown_fields
finding: Test payloads sent 'name' and 'display_name', which serde silently drops. The payload reads as if it exercised fields that do not exist, and would 422 (still passing the loose assertion) if deny_unknown_fields were ever added.
resolution: fixed — payloads reduced to the declared fields in both test files

finding: spawn_idle_reaper doc still read 'Called once from main.rs' after the change moved the call into library code — the exact stale-comment class this change set out to eliminate.
resolution: fixed by the reaper decision above (it IS main.rs-only again, so the sentence is true), plus an added note that it currently reaps nothing and why it is not started on the embedded path

finding: Re-export comment said 'used via full module path in main.rs and handlers'; core::app_builder is now also a consumer.
resolution: fixed — comment updated

finding: No Option<McpConfig> deploy-level kill-switch for the mcp module (CODING_GUIDELINES §16), so the installer's side effects are ungated on every path.
resolution: not actioned — pre-existing for the main.rs path and moot after the reaper was removed from the shared path: install_mcp_session_manager now has no background side effect, only construction plus a layer. Adding an mcp kill-switch is a separate change with its own surface.

finding: The global() half of INV-1 has no executable test on the desktop assembly — three consumers (agent-host resolver, workflow agent_dispatch, agent_tool_call) would fail with 'MCP session manager not initialized' and nothing would catch it. Pinned only by a structural argument.
resolution: not actioned — recorded as a follow-up in TESTS.md. FIX_ROUND-1 strengthened the argument from line-ordering to a by-construction identity (the Extension can only carry what global() returns), but that is still not executable. A workflow kind:tool step test on start_desktop() would close it; judged disproportionate for a LIGHT-tier fix and named rather than silently dropped.

finding: set_global now runs ~120 lines later in main.rs (after router assembly rather than before it), widening the window in which global() returns None.
resolution: not actioned — traced and found theoretical: every global() reader is request- or dispatch-driven, and the only boot-spawned task in that window (workflow startup_sweep::sweep_at_boot) fails stale runs without dispatching. Module init, which spawns the boot tasks, already ran before BOTH the old and new positions.

finding: Layer ordering across the split method chain — checked byte-for-byte in both main.rs and lib.rs.
resolution: no defect — the new call occupies the exact slot the old inline .layer(Extension(..)) held; cors remains the last .layer() and therefore outermost; Extension layers are order-independent among themselves

finding: Borrow/move/scope of module_context and config across the new call site.
resolution: no defect — module_context is only ever borrowed (constructed lib.rs:529, borrowed at :537/:587/:677); app is re-bound by shadowing, which is legal; compiler-enforced regardless

oracle: mutation analysis: layering Arc::new(McpSessionManager::new(cfg)) directly in lib.rs passes all four route tests while leaving global() unset
finding: The set_global half of INV-1 was pinned only by a prose coupling argument, and that argument guards the wrong mutation. The dangerous edit is a future lib.rs that layers a manager WITHOUT going through build_session_manager — green tests, original defect restored for every global() consumer.
resolution: fixed — TEST-4 added as an in-source unit test asserting Arc::ptr_eq(build_session_manager(..), global()) plus idempotency. The earlier 'Config has no Default' objection was wrong: Config derives Deserialize and all non-flattened fields are serde(default), so a minimal serde_json fixture builds one

oracle: an unmounted route answers 404 with an EMPTY body, which satisfied both the old assert_eq!(NOT_FOUND) and every !body.contains(..) check
finding: The comment claimed asserting 404 stops a removed route passing — it does the opposite: a route-miss 404 also passes. TESTS.md repeated the same false claim. A documented-but-absent guarantee is worse than a gap because the next reader trusts it.
resolution: fixed — TEST-2 now uses a non-admin and asserts 403 + USER_NO_ACCESS, a code only the handler body produces. Route-miss (404/405, empty body) fails both assertions. TESTS.md corrected

oracle: file header claims it 'mirrors the desktop assertions route-for-route'; both exact-status assertions were absent
finding: The standalone test did not mirror the desktop one — its status pins were missing, so unmounting either route or stubbing the handler left it green, contradicting its own header.
resolution: fixed — both assert_eq! status pins and the body-code assertions copied across; the header claim is now true

oracle: has_admin_access (runtime.rs:49-63) returns true for ANY mcp_servers_admin::* perm, including ::create
finding: Both tests granted mcp_servers_admin::create to BOTH users, so the 'user' in TEST-2 was an MCP admin and can_user_access_server was skipped entirely. The ownership branch was untested by construction, and the expected status was coupled to the exact contents of MCP_ADMIN_PERMISSIONS.
resolution: fixed — permissions split into ADMIN_PERMS and READ_PERMS in both files; TEST-2 now runs as a genuine non-admin and asserts the ownership refusal, removing the bypass and the brittle coupling

finding: PRE_HANDLER_REJECTIONS was sold as exhaustive but omitted USER_NOT_FOUND (401) and USER_INACTIVE (403), which also short-circuit before the Extension extractor.
resolution: fixed — both codes added in each file

finding: The idempotent early-return silently pins the FIRST config forever; a second boot after a jwt.secret rotation would keep minting under the stale secret. Fails closed, but invisible.
resolution: fixed — tracing::warn! on the already-installed branch stating that the passed config is ignored

oracle: the closure re-applies exactly Extension(jwt) + CORS onto merged desktop routes; grep confirms no desktop route uses McpSessionManager today
finding: The desktop route-builder closure drops every parent layer except the two it re-applies. A desktop-owned route declaring Extension<Arc<McpSessionManager>> would 500 with the identical rejection. Latent, untested, and the file's own comment says merge drops parent layers without naming this consequence.
resolution: fixed (documented) — note added at the merge seam naming the MCP extension specifically and what to do if a desktop route ever needs it. Not code-fixed: no desktop route uses it, and pre-emptively re-applying an unused extension would be dead wiring

oracle: verified all three legs myself: run_in_sandbox:false hardcoded (test_connection.rs:176); HOST_ALLOWED_COMMANDS gates the COMMAND only with args copied verbatim (stdio.rs:27, :365-371); mcp_servers::create granted to the 'Users' system group (202607146065_mcp_grant_permissions.sql:6-8)
finding: POST /mcp/servers/test-connection with transport stdio spawns an unsandboxed host process. Any registered user can supply command=python3, args=[-c, payload]. Pre-existing and live on the standalone binary; this change makes it reachable on the DESKTOP process, which remote_access/ngrok can publish to the internet.
resolution: NOT fixed here — pre-existing defect in test_connection/stdio, not introduced by this change, and the decision to gate/harden vs ship is the owner's. Escalated in the PR body and the STATUS file rather than shipped silently. This change's real security character is that the 500 was accidentally fail-closed on desktop.

finding: test-connection over http performs no handler-level validate_outbound_url and the client policy MCP_USER permits loopback/RFC1918, making the 200 body a reachability oracle for the desktop's loopback ports and the user's LAN. Companion findings: stored decrypted header/env secrets can be exfiltrated via {is_secret:true,value:null} plus an attacker-controlled url (no url-match guard, unlike resolve_oauth); get_or_create_with_context uses get_any_server with no ownership scoping; no env_clear()/PR_SET_PDEATHSIG on spawned stdio children.
resolution: NOT fixed here — all pre-existing, all newly REACHABLE on desktop because of this change. Grouped and escalated with the item above; each is its own change with its own review.
